impact.rationale: The sidecar is a durable authority for automated refresh attempts. A definite pre-rename failure can leave process memory ahead of durable bytes, and the exported reservation pointer can mutate capacity authority outside the store lock.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The contradictions follow directly from Go slice and pointer aliasing at every affected call; one newly authored v4 source test is itself incompatible with the implementation and should fail when executed.

regressionProtection.rationale: The patch adds useful definite/uncertain cut and state-shape tests, but the definite-completion test exposes the shallow-copy defect, the bind test omits in-memory and reopen assertions, and no actual Go test was run.

recoverability.rationale: A source fix can deep-clone snapshots and detached views and add bounded definite-write retry policy. Existing uncertain-write poison and reopen semantics can remain intact, but persisted state may otherwise require controlled restart and inspection.

confidence.rationale: The main findings are deterministic from the frozen afterimage: slice assignment shares backing arrays, RefreshView copies share Reservation pointers, and the worker call chain returns on the first sidecar error.

applicability.rationale: The reviewed patch and all 24 manifest afterimages match the frozen candidate, reverse-apply succeeds, and the contradicted paths are the actual RefreshStore and server runtime paths introduced by P207A.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Integrating v4 as written would advertise exact retry after definite persistence failure while allowing memory/disk divergence and would terminate the whole runtime for definite sidecar errors not absorbed by finishRefresh.

riskDrivers: refreshSnapshot shallow-copies mutable slices and RefreshView reservation pointers
public read and claim results expose the same Reservation pointer held by store state
KnownNotCommitted persistence errors are not uniformly retried by the runtime caller
snapshot validation accepts a positive AttemptSequence below its ledger high-water
protectiveFactors: pre-rename and post-rename disk failures are distinguished
uncertain commits poison the process-local store and require reopen
the main subscription-store/v1 wire remains separate
UNKNOWN retains capacity ownership and does not auto-retry

materialBoundaries.invariant: A pre-rename definite failure leaves durable bytes, process memory, and opaque capability state unchanged so the same operation can perform a real durable retry.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: BindCommand, Complete, RotateCheckpoint, observe, claim, and reconciliation start from n := s.state. Refreshes and Ledgers therefore share backing arrays with s.state. Mutating n.Refreshes or n.Ledgers changes s.state before persist; beforeRename then returns CodeStoreUnsafe with disk bytes unchanged. A Bind retry sees the in-memory CommandID and skips persist, while a Complete retry sees a terminal state and conflicts.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Deep-clone IdentityKey, Ledgers, Refreshes, and every Reservation before mutation; assign only the detached successfully persisted value. Test each mutator with a definite cut, exact in-memory and durable preimage equality, proof that retry reaches persist again, and close/reopen equality.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Read and claim APIs return detached data plus only the intended opaque lease; callers cannot mutate store capacity authority without the store lock and persist path.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: RefreshView is copied by value but contains *RefreshReservation. Refreshes appends v directly and claim returns v directly, so callers receive the same reservation object referenced by s.state.Refreshes. Changing its slots or bytes changes in-memory ReservedCapacity without validation, persistence, or locking.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Clone Reservation on every snapshot clone and every outward RefreshView copy. Keep Lease process-local and add mutation-after-return tests proving internal state and durable bytes remain unchanged.

materialBoundaries.invariant: A definite sidecar persistence failure is either recovered in-process without replaying network or main-store effects, or the contract accurately declares that the refresh worker and HTTP runtime stop.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: finishRefresh invokes Complete once. refreshOnce returns any resulting error; RunRefresh returns on the first RefreshOnce error; startWorker converts that return into workerErrors; RunWith then closes the HTTP server. Direct store tests demonstrate a same-capability API retry but the actual caller does not perform it for Complete, observe, top-level Refreshes, or ClaimLive persistence failures.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: After fixing snapshot isolation, add a bounded same-stage retry for definite sidecar writes while holding the same attempt/critical section and without rerunning fetch or main-store effects. Keep uncertain writes poison-and-stop. Alternatively declare definite local persistence errors fatal and remove any same-process self-heal claim.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Every persisted positive AttemptSequence equals that source ledger's LastIssuedSequence; only an idle or pre-attempt sequence-blocked view may sit below retained ledger history.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: Validation only rejects AttemptSequence greater than LastIssuedSequence. A canonical running or terminal view with AttemptSequence 1 and the same source ledger at 2 is accepted even though claim is the only producer of positive attempts and always advances both to the same sequence.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Require equality whenever AttemptSequence is positive and retain the existing zero-sequence exception for idle and sequence-exhausted blocked states. Add reopen negatives for lower view sequence in Running, terminal, and UNKNOWN states.

materialBoundaries.invariant: An after-rename uncertain write poisons the live store, forbids replay, and requires reopen to classify the bytes found on disk.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: No source counterexample found in the reviewed v4 delta; persist marks poisoned when write reports uncertain, and later usable calls reject.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Retain poison-before-retry and reopen tests on actual Linux after integration.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Automation state remains in the separately versioned sidecar and does not add an Automated field to the main subscription-store/v1 persisted wire.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: No wire-field counterexample found in the 24-path Go-only patch; v4 changes only refresh.go and refresh_test.go relative to v3.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Retain the strict legacy decode and exact-head Linux compatibility tests after final overlay.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Long-running scheduled refresh remains bounded while preserving Accepted LKV, manual records, UNKNOWN/inflight authority, approval references, and anti-replay high-water state.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: subscription main store and refresh sidecar
materialBoundaries.counterexample: The delivery explicitly does not implement the durable sealed history/archive and active-store compaction slice; fixed capacity still eventually fails closed.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Design and separately validate bounded retention/compaction before claiming module completion; it is not required to pretend this Go-only source slice is complete.
